description_full: Roblox Corporation operates an immersive platform for connection and communication in the United States and internationally. It offers Roblox Client, an application that allows users to explore immersive experience; Roblox Studio, a free toolset that allows developers and creators to build, publish, and operate immersive experiences and other content; and Roblox Cloud, which provides services and infrastructure that power the platform. Roblox Corporation was incorporated in 2004 and is headquartered in San Mateo, California.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 3K people. Revenue per employee of $1.6M ranks in the top quartile among Communication Services peers, improving at 26%/yr — growing workforce leverage. Each employee generates $442K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $368K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 1× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags elevated compensation governance risk (10/10).
financial_summary: Roblox Corporation is a large-cap communication services business with a $35.3B market cap on $4.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +30% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
The business throws off $1.4B in free cash flow — roughly 28 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
Accruals are elevated at -29.9% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, thin -29.7× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 0.3% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and stock-based comp at 23% of revenue is silent dilution an owner has to account for, and insiders hold 3.5% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
